AccessComputing Webinar: Improving Information Access for Scientific Documents

UW Tacoma Events

Scientific knowledge is only meaningful if people can access, understand, and make use of it. Although open access has removed paywalls for many scientific papers, many barriers remain. Papers may be inaccessible to people using assistive technologies, difficult for non-specialists to understand, or hard to translate into practical applications. Emerging AI technologies create new opportunities to study these challenges at scale and develop tools that improve access, but these transformations also introduce risks around information fidelity and the communication of uncertainty. CCDPM Legacy Lecture: Inclusion, Exclusion and Porn: Centring (inter)subjective experiences in health-science scholarship

UBC Okanagan Events

The Centre for Chronic Disease Prevention and Management (CCDPM) is pleased to announce our next Legacy Lecture Series presentation at UBC Okanagan. Dr. Justin Haegele presents Inclusion, Exclusion, and Porn: Centring (inter)subjective experiences in health-science scholarship. Dr. Haegele will focus on inclusion and exclusion as (inter)subjective experiences, and the implications these conceptualizations have for health research. He will explore concepts related to epistemic injustice and inclusion porn, and discuss challenges in the field in which the concept of inclusion is used, sometimes without thinking about the needs, wants, and desires of people with disabilities. Bio Justin A. Haeg

Writing for Graduate Success: Mastering the Literature Review

Centre for Writing and Scholarly Communication

A strong literature review is more than a summary; it’s a scholarly conversation that positions your research within the field. However, writing a literature review can feel like navigating a maze of research. Join this practical, research-informed workshop to discover common structures and strategies for writing literature reviews that are purposeful, precise, and aligned with disciplinary expectations. announcedEngineering & Science

HMSC Research Seminar: Bowhead whales in a changing Arctic

Oregon State University Events

Speaker: Kate Stafford, Associate Professor, Marine Mammal Institute, Oregon State University Topic: Bowhead whales are the only baleen whale endemic to the Arctic. As such, they have numerous unique adaptations to living in the ice. Because of this habitat, they can be very difficult to study in below freezing temperatures and during polar night. However, novel tools, including passive acoustic monitoring, have given scientists a window into the dark icy world of the bowhead. This world is changing rapidly and declines in sea ice are changing the behavior of bowhead whales and introducing new threats and competitors into the Arctic.
